Hi Tam,

Thanks for putting this tool together. 

I have tested it out a little and have a few questions/suggestions:

-From the current help, it is unclear whether there is a warmup period
-I noticed some file types are not supported, such as .res and .pnd?
-Your documentation mentions that we should be able to continue simulations if they are interrupted, but I was not able to do this. It would also be great to be able to open a fresh session and load outputs from simulations that have completed without having to go back to step 1. If this is already possible, a tutorial would be very helpful. 

I am interested in the online meeting, depending on what time it will be scheduled.

All the best,

Danica

messages.author: e28329d3e25e358e
messages.subject: Re: Online meeting - tutorial how to use SWATshiny for SWAT calibration/sensitivity/uncertainty analyis
parts:
Hi all,

Sorry for cross-posting. I just want to say that the issues raised by Danica have been solved and the code was already updated in GitHub

1) Q: From the current help, it is unclear whether there is a warmup period:
     A: The program automatically reads these information from the "file.cio" and allows you to select the calibration time only after the warm-up period
2) Q: I noticed some file types are not supported, such as .res and .pnd?
    A: modifying parameters from .res and .pnd are now possible, just treat these parameters as other subbasin-scale parameters (e.g., like CH_K2.rte parameter in the example)
3) Q: Your documentation mentions that we should be able to continue simulations .....
    A: Restart option is now possible (See step 3. Run SWAT => 6. Load previous results (optional - for loading previous results))

NOTICE: I am happy that many people are interested in the online meeting. I will address these issues in the meeting.
                If you worry about your privacy, please don't put your email address in your answer, as a group owner I can see your email, otherwise you can send your email address privately to me

Thanks
Tam
